cells.tense: You are keeping the thing that grew out of hard work alive, and the nod can come without you chasing it.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Give ordinary upkeep to something that grew out of work you carried, and never ask anyone to notice it.
cells.core:
You know what a thing costs, and you can hold to it beyond the mark where other people stop. What grows where you look after it is allowed to grow without being pushed, and you can hold room for the other person without holding on. When the hard work is finished and someone says so, you take it in, and the connection stays yours to give.

Care that doesn't exhaust is what carries this. Give ordinary upkeep to one thing that grew from work you carried — not a bigger push, just tending. What is alive gets kept without clutching. That upkeep is the whole instruction; asking is not part of it. The part of the connection that bends when effort goes unreceived can sit a week without you fracturing it to reach for thanks.

cells.tense: You will carry the next thing so cleanly that they cannot miss what it costs, and outrun the slower rhythm of being seen.
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Take the list you are holding for other people and strike one item off that does not serve — no replacement.
cells.core:
Feeling with people rather than just about them is what you do well, and here it has turned outward into proving the sacrifice: the bearing is cleaner, the load carried further, the receipt demanded sooner. Done right, finishing ends in ease — not a loss — not in an encore nobody requested. The faster you run past when others can notice, the more invisible the work gets, and the more you pour in to make it land.

What pulls you back is refining what you perceive. Strike one thing from the list that does not serve. Look at what you are holding for other people, cross off one item that will not be missed, and then stand firm with that crossed line. Sharpening serves growth, not worry. One item is enough; the wish to be told can stay in your hand instead of steering the load.
cells.sheetLine: You're racing past the slower rhythm of being seen
cells.verb: Being seen for the weight you took on

cells.tense: You carried the weight quietly and stood at the door after the going was already done.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Stand firm in the hardship of this week exactly as it comes, without looking around to see who noticed before you set it down.
cells.core:
The place where two people meet goes quiet on your side when the work has gone unseen. You stay at the door after the walking is done, and the connection sits present but unreceived. What you sacrificed for has not been said by the person holding it, and the room where that would happen stays thinner than it needs to be. This was once a place you could stand in and simply be met.

What steadies you is standing where the pressure lands. Stand firm in the material hardship. Hold the week as it comes on what you have in you, without looking around to see who noticed before you set it down. What you have is yours, not evidence to be filed. Don't push effort or feeling into the thin part directly — let standing where you are be enough.

cells.tense: The connection is kept alive by you, and by your account it is simply how the two of you happen to be.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Look after one thing between you and someone else with a steady hand, and hold in your own mind that this care comes from you.
cells.core:
What is carried between you and other people is kept moving — the load redistributed, the moment held open, the sacrifice made smooth enough not to notice. Nobody else has been told where it comes from, and your own account says the connection simply runs this way. What you gave up for these people is real and working, and the one thing it has not reached is your own recognition of it.

Start with one piece. Look after what grows with a steady hand — one thing between you and someone else, kept steady the way you keep the rest. Then hold this in your own mind: what you are doing is yours. You don't have to tell anyone. Done right, this ends in release arriving on its own from finishing, and here release is your own awareness of the work, not more work.
